title: streaming SSE chunking/backpressure debug notes
content:
Context / symptom:
- Intermittent stalls observed while streaming long model responses over SSE (hosted API). Client sees initial data then large pauses (10s-30s) before more chunks arrive. Occasionally client shows complete stall until TCP FIN.
- Affects some customer routes more heavily (longer prefix tokens, frequent small tokens). Suspect chunking/flushing behavior + proxy buffering + client backpressure interaction.

Where seen:
- Hosted API (frontend load balancer -> envoy gateway -> model-worker).
- Repro on local dev using simple server that flushes small SSE messages every 50ms.

What I've tried (commands + quick results):
1) Basic curl test against our dev server (no proxies):
- server: node/express SSE test that flushes "data: x\n\n" every 50ms.
- curl -N http://localhost:3000/sse | sed -n '1,10p'
  -> shows steady stream, no stalls locally.

2) Test through envoy locally (simulating gateway):
- docker-compose with envoy config that proxies to local server.
- curl -N http://localhost:9901/sse | ts
  -> intermittent pauses matching production symptom (~10-20s).
  -> envoy logs show connection open, but no logs for writes (server continues writing).

3) Repro with python requests stream (to inspect raw bytes):
- python snippet:
  import requests
  r = requests.get(url, stream=True)
  for chunk in r.iter_content(chunk_size=None):
      print(repr(chunk))
- Observed: sometimes iter_content returns b'' for long periods (requests waiting for underlying socket).

4) Node fetch readable stream test (browser-like):
- const res = await fetch(url); const reader = res.body.getReader(); 
  while(true) { const {value, done} = await reader.read(); console.log(value); }
- Reader.read() stalls similarly when routed through gateway.

5) tcpdump on worker -> shows data being sent from worker to envoy consistently (small packets ~80-200 bytes with ~50ms spacing).
- tcpdump between envoy and client shows larger aggregated packets delivered less frequently (bursts).

6) Nginx buffering test (turned on proxy_buffering on/off):
- With proxy_buffering off, fewer stalls. With buffering on, bursts appear.

7) AB experiments: varying chunk size / server flush cadence
- Increasing flush size to ~1KB reduces stalls drastically. Very small writes (<=200B) more likely to stall.

Error snippets / logs:
- Envoy stats: upstream_rq_time_bucket shows long tails.
- Worker stdout: "wrote 128 bytes" every 50ms (expected).
- Netstat shows ESTABLISHED; no resets.
- No obvious 5xx errors in gateway.

Hypotheses:
1) Proxy/server side Nagle-like coalescing + proxy buffering: small writes are being coalesced by kernel/TCP stack or buffered by the gateway causing bursts. (Evidence: tcpdump shows packets sent but gateway aggregates).
2) Envoy (or intermediate LB) applies buffering / flow control with a waterline: if downstream (client) is slow, envoy may stop flushing to client and then backpressure the upstream only after its buffer exceeds high watermark; until then we perceive stalls.
3) HTTP/2 vs HTTP/1.1 difference: some layers convert protocol and introduce buffering. If client is using http/2, intermediate translation could cause reassembly delays.
4) Chunk framing semantics / missing final newline in SSE messages cause some clients/gateways to not flush until newline or blank line.
5) TLS/ALPN interactions or TLS record sizing causing aggregation.

Immediate reproducer steps (minimal):
A) Local node SSE server (server.js):
- express + keep-alive, setHeader('Content-Type','text/event-stream'), res.flushHeaders();
- setInterval(() => { res.write(`data: ${Date.now()}\n\n`); }, 50);
- run: node server.js

B) Repro variants:
1) Direct curl (no proxy): curl -N http://localhost:3000/sse   # baseline working
2) Through envoy: curl -N http://localhost:9901/sse   # reproduces pause
3) With larger writes: modify server to write 1KB chunks every 50ms and test again -> less stalls
4) Turn on nginx proxy_buffering (proxy_buffering on;) and test -> stalls appear

Commands used to inspect networking:
- tcpdump -i lo -s 0 -w /tmp/sse.pcap port 3000 or host 127.0.0.1
- sudo ss -tanp | grep 9901  # check socket queues
- strace -f -e write -p <worker-pid>  # watch write syscalls timing

Observations from strace:
- worker write() syscalls returning quickly ~50ms spacing (server thinks it wrote).
- write syscall sizes small and consistent.

Envoy config knobs tried:
- upstream_flow_control_enabled: false (no change)
- downstream_flow_control_enabled: false (reduced stalls in local tests)
- use_remote_address: true/false (no impact)
- enable_retries false (no impact)

Notes about clients:
- Chrome's EventSource seems tolerant (buffers more) but still shows UI-level stalls.
- curl -N will print immediately but might be subject to buffering in terminal emulator (use -s).

Potential mitigations / temporary fixes:
- Increase server-side flush size (bundle small tokens into 1KB frames) as a pragmatic workaround for customers on gateways that buffer.
- Add SSE comment heartbeats (":\n\n") every 1s to force flush; however, some gateways still coalesce small writes.
- For dedicated routes, configure gateway/proxy to disable buffering for SSE endpoints (proxy_buffering off / chunked transfer hints).
- Add an opt-in header like x-redwood-streaming-hint: chunked-flush to instruct gateways to apply no-buffering policy (requires infra change).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Is this specific to Envoy version X? Need to test with envoy 1.25 vs 1.30. Samir to try.
- Confirm whether ALB/CloudFront in front of hosted API might be doing additional aggregation. Need customer request tracing.
- Add unit/integration tests that run envoy in front of a fake worker and measure per-message latency under tiny writes.
- Investigate kernel TCP_NODELAY behavior on our worker containers. Ensure socket setNoDelay(true) is applied before writes.

Action items:
- [ ] Samir: run envoy version matrix tests (1.24..1.30) and report differences (JIRA-RED-2241).
- [ ] Ava: add flaky e2e test that fails when median per-chunk latency > 150ms for 50ms server cadence.
- [ ] Jordan: prototype "flush bundle" in runtime: buffer up to 1KB or 200ms then write as one chunk. Measure cost on latency.
- [ ] Noah: verify cloud LB behavior for SSE routes and whether TLS records are being coalesced.

Notes-to-self: keep this doc as the primary scratchpad; convert to a formal postmortem if a customer-facing incident is filed.

References / links:
- https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/faq/http2_vs_http1
- https://www.nginx.com/blog/benefits-of-buffering/
- https://github.com/expressjs/compression/issues/119  (notes on flush behavior)

Recent experiment results (2024-10-30):
- Bundle writes into 1KB -> P95 chunk latency drops from ~1.2s to ~80ms across gateway.
- Added socket.setNoDelay(true) on worker -> small improvement but not sufficient alone.

If you pick this up: start with reproducer through envoy + tcpdump and confirm whether envoy is reassembling/ buffering blocks. If envoy is aggregating, test downstream_flow_control toggles and downstream window sizes.

End of notes.
